thread:
customer_acme: hey team — starting ~10:05 UTC we saw a spike of 429s on the embeddings endpoint, plus tail latency jumped from ~120ms to 1.8s before the 429s. no config change on our side. any pointers?

alice_support: sorry about that — can you paste a sample request id and the app_id? also roughly how much qps were you sending to embeddings?

customer_acme: app_id: acme-payments-prod, sample req id: req_0a3f9c2f. traffic was steady ~45 qps for last 2 hours, bursty peaks to ~120 qps for ~30s every 5m.

alice_support: thanks. forwarding to infra, adding logs. bryan, can you take a look? tagging @bryan_engineer

bryan_engineer: looking. quick glance at platform logs shows a cascade: many requests hit high batch queueing, KV-prefetch tasks ramped up, and the per-worker token quota hit a cooldown window leading to 429s. this looks like perceived throttling rather than hard account quota exhaustion.

customer_acme: "per-worker token quota" — can you explain? we have a reserved capacity plan, shouldn't this be stable?

bryan_engineer: reserved capacity helps but we still enforce soft per-worker rate limits and continuous batching windows to protect latency SLOs. when background prefetch + concurrent client bursts align, a lot of tokens are consumed in short windows on a subset of workers, which triggers the local backpressure/cooldown. that shows as client 429s even though global committed capacity isn't fully used.

mira_oncall: adding a quick repro snippet for what we saw in the logs — the worker queue length spikes and kernel time goes up:```
[2024-05-28T10:05:12Z] worker=rt-42 queue_len=68 batch_size=16 kv_prefetch=12 kernel_ms=320
[2024-05-28T10:05:13Z] worker=rt-42 quota_cooldown=true cooldown_until=2024-05-28T10:05:18Z
```

alice_support: ok actionable items: bryan, can we get the per-worker throttle traces? customer, while we look, can you try one change client-side: reduce client-side max_concurrency to 20 and add a linear retry with jitter for 429s for 10s? that should smooth the perceived throttling.

customer_acme: sure we can test that. do you recommend any server-side config?

bryan_engineer: on our side we pushed a short-term mitigation: lowered continuous-batch-window from 200ms -> 120ms for that worker pool and enabled kv-warmup-smoothing for the embeddings model variant. that reduces bursty token spikes from prefetch. we also raised per-worker soft quota threshold by 15% for the next hour to let traffic drain.

deploy-bot: rollout started by bryan_engineer: rollout_id=rl-9072; targets=embeddings-pool-eu; strategy=canary; 5 -> 20%

customer_acme: testing with client-side changes now. initial result: request latency back to ~140-220ms and no 429s in the last 90s. will keep running for 10m. thanks.

bryan_engineer: great — for a longer-term fix: 1) consider smoothing your client traffic (reduce micro-bursting), 2) enable our Optimize suggestion "kv-prefetch-budgeting" (it staggers prefetches), 3) if you need frequent short bursts, we can add a small burst-capacity add-on to the contract. I'll open a follow-up ticket with recommended config and dashboard charts.

alice_support: ticket created: SUP-9421 — bryan please attach traces and the exact worker IDs. customer_acme if you confirm stability we'll close the thread. :thumbsup:

customer_acme: looks stable after 12m — no 429s and smoother latency. thanks everyone. appreciate the quick fix.

bryan_engineer: attached traces to SUP-9421 and documented the param changes we rolled. follow-up: we'll schedule a short runbook update about "per-worker perceived throttling" and include best-practice client knobs.

mira_oncall: note for oncall rotation — if you see embeddings 429s + queue_len >50 and kernel_ms >250ms, consider lowering continuous-batch-window by 30-40% and enable kv-warmup-smoothing for the affected pool.

customer_acme: one last q — will the short-term per-worker quota bump be permanent?

bryan_engineer: no, it was temporary to let the burst finish. we'll revert to previous thresholds after traffic stabilizes; long-term we'll provision either burst capacity or change batching profiles based on your workload patterns. I'll include options in SUP-9421.

customer_acme: perfect. closing on our end once you revert.

alice_support: marking this thread resolved pending SUP-9421 follow-up. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
